bio: Marvin is a Head of Content with 8+ years in finance, FX/CFD, crypto, and Web3. At mb.io, the crypto exchange arm of MultiBank Group, he runs three brand accounts off one calendar: the exchange, the $MBG Token, and the CEO's personal brand. Under that calendar sit the social posts, the long-form editorial, the earn campaigns, the paid ad copy, the client comms, and the market research that feeds all of it.

Because Web3 still runs on rooms as much as feeds, part of the job happens on the floor. He was lead organizer of the mb.io Platinum Sponsor booth at Istanbul Blockchain Week 2026: he worked the vendors and event organizers end to end, ran KOL relations, and shot content on site. Same brief at Binance Blockchain Week, RWA Week Dubai, Bitcoin Pizza Day at TheBlock, and Philippine Blockchain Week.

Behind all of that sits the tooling. He built the mb.io content dashboard in-role, and Cryptopedia, the exchange's crypto knowledge base, now runs past 100 entries against a 300+ topic roadmap, all of it written to rank in search and get quoted back by chatbots.

On paper: an MBA in Digital Marketing from King's Business School and a BFA in Creative Writing from Ateneo de Manila University, which is a polite way of saying he has been professionally overthinking words since 2014.
He has ADHD. Most of what is above came out of hyperfocus, and he stopped apologizing for that years ago.

Off the clock he is usually underwater (licensed scuba and cave diver), underground (spelunker), or somewhere in his 30th-odd country with no particular agenda. He lives in Dubai. The plants are still alive, which he counts as a win.

funFacts.label: Built an AI content dashboard in-role

howIWork.heading: AI-native, by default
paragraphs: I build the tools I run content with. Three brand accounts and eleven content pillars with no full content team meant the calendar had to live somewhere better than a spreadsheet, so I shipped the mb.io Content Dashboard on Google AI Studio, Firebase, and Claude Code: scheduling with approval layers, a writing agent trained per brand voice, a blog manager running a 100+ topic roadmap, and gap detection that flags a pillar before it goes quiet.

The same habit shows up everywhere else. AI video production runs through Higgsfield and Kling, agentic workflows through Claude Code, and monitoring pipelines turn crypto, macro, and real-world asset feeds into a weekly Monday Outlook. Cryptopedia came out of the same instinct: 100+ articles answering the questions people actually type, built to be quoted by search engines and chatbots alike.
